section_summary: This section contains consular reports and related State Department memoranda and correspondence concerning economic developments in Japanese-ruled Taiwan during 1930 and early 1931. The primary documents are two detailed reports by Vice Consul Charles S. Reed II examining the Taiwan Government General's enforcement of a domestic industries campaign that effectively boycotted foreign goods, and detailing Japan's coordinated policy of utilizing Taiwan as a stepping stone for economic penetration into South China and Southeast Asia through subsidized bank loans and trade expansion. Subsequent Department of State memoranda and correspondence document the evaluation and interagency distribution of the South Seas report to the Office of Naval Intelligence, Military Intelligence Division, Bureau of Foreign and Domestic Commerce, Bureau of Insular Affairs, and the Governor General of the Philippine Islands.

subfiles.about: A voluntary consular report detailing the Taiwan Government General's adoption and strict enforcement of Tokyo's buy-domestic policy and its detrimental effects on foreign and American trade.
subfiles.from: Charles S. Reed II, American Vice Consul, Taihoku, Taiwan
subfiles.summary: Vice Consul Charles S. Reed II reports on the Taiwan Government General's aggressive implementation of Japan's national policy encouraging the use of domestic products, which has created a virtual boycott of foreign goods. Governmental bodies and private purchasing associations strictly require Japanese goods regardless of price or quality, posing serious obstacles to American commerce in Taiwan. The report analyzes commercial reactions, obstacles including local consumer preference for foreign goods and confusing foreign-language labeling on domestic manufactures, and notes that American products retain significant prestige despite the official campaign.
subfiles.title: Taiwan Adopts the National Policy of Fostering Domestic Industries and Manufactures

subfiles.about: A Division of Far Eastern Affairs memorandum summarizing Vice Consul Reed's report on Japanese economic penetration in the South Seas and recommending its circulation to military, naval, and commerce officials.
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Summarizes Vice Consul Reed's report on Japanese economic penetration in the South Seas, noting Kanan Bank loans to Mindanao plantations and recommending distribution to Commerce, O.N.I., and M.I.D.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Voluntary Report 'Taiwan and the South Seas'
subfiles.to: Stanley K. Hornbeck, Chief, Division of Far Eastern Affairs

subfiles.about: A comprehensive confidential report detailing Japan's coordinated policy of economic, commercial, and financial penetration into South China and the South Seas using Taiwan as an operational base.
subfiles.from: Charles S. Reed II, American Vice Consul, Taihoku, Taiwan
subfiles.summary: Vice Consul Charles S. Reed II provides an in-depth analysis of Japan's strategic use of Taiwan as a springboard for economic penetration into South China and Southeast Asia. The report exposes a confidential revolving credit scheme operated through the Kanan Ginko and Bank of Taiwan with government interest subsidies from the 'Nanshi Nanyo Shisetsuhi' fund to finance Japanese plantations and enterprises in Malaya, Sumatra, and Mindanao. It further examines commercial groundwork including specialized Dutch language instruction and regional research in Taiwan schools, shipping subsidies, Japanese dominance in South Seas fisheries, and rising political tension among native populations in Davao.
subfiles.title: Taiwan and the South Seas
